claim: Lateriser will definitely activate a bonus chip (Free Hit or Wildcard) this gameweek because he has already made several squad changes in the last 2-3 days and would otherwise take a big points hit; he is leaning 60% Free Hit, 40% Wildcard.
quote: I think I'm 60% leaning towards Free Hit and 40% towards Wildcard. I've already made a few substitutions in the last 2-3 days, so I'll definitely use the bonus, otherwise I'll have to subtract 20 points.

claim: Jack (host) says he is exactly 50/50 between Free Hit and Wildcard this week for his own team, having already made seven or eight transfers without activating either chip.
quote: I've already made seven or eight transfers. Haven't activated the bonus yet, but will have to use Free Hit or Wildcard. I'm exactly 50/50 right now.

claim: Lateriser argues the Free Hit chip is specifically for a week when a great fixture comes up for a team whose players you don't currently own, and that his squad composition being 'on the edge' (one free transfer, defensive injury problems) makes this the right week for it.
quote: I believe that the 'free hit' chip is needed when, say, a great match comes up for a team whose players you don't have... I wanted to use the chip this week because, you know, my composition is on the edge.

claim: Lateriser considers the Wildcard the most powerful chip of the first half of the season and says he would rather delay it two or three weeks to build the squad correctly, even taking some transfer hits in the meantime, than rush it before December when free transfers reset.
quote: I think it's better to take a few penalty points for transfers in the first two or three weeks, but make sure you build the team... it's okay if I delay the decision for two or three weeks to be confident in my team.

claim: Lateriser says he looked at a Gameweek 12 Free Hit window (banking on Arsenal vs Man City) but found the fixture unattractive, and instead rates Chelsea's home game vs Hull (Hull have a high underlying xGC despite not conceding) and Liverpool at home to Fulham (Fulham have created the most big chances in the league this season) as the standout Free Hit opportunities this week.
quote: I thought Chelsea's home game against Hull, although they haven't conceded a goal, has 5 xGC, and Liverpool's home game against Fulham, which has created the most big chances in the league this season, was a good opportunity.

claim: Lateriser lists an injured Rodon as one of the squad problems pushing him toward using his chip this week.
quote: I have an injured Rodon.

claim: Lateriser is leaving Maguire out this week because Man Utd play away at Man City.
quote: I have Maguire, who plays against City.

claim: Lateriser flags O'Reilly's fitness as still unclear going into the weekend, one of the reasons pushing him toward the chip.
quote: O'Reilly's health is still unclear.

claim: Jack (host) asks whether the 60/40 Free Hit lean is really driven by O'Reilly's fitness doubt or by Lateriser's actual Gameweek 5 squad strength; Lateriser says it is more the latter -- he rates his own GW5 team highly on the assumption O'Reilly is fit.
quote: This would be a more weighty factor in favoring me to choose the 'free hit' earlier, because I have a pretty decent team for the fifth round.

claim: Lateriser likes Calvert-Lewin as a lightly-owned differential for Leeds' home game against Newcastle in Gameweek 5.
quote: Calvert-Lewin against Newcastle... You like it as a differential. Few will have it before the start of the 5th round.

claim: Lateriser is watching Man City's midweek cup match against Norwich for clues on rotation before Gameweek 5 against Sunderland, expecting Maresca-style patterns where players rested in the cup then start in the league; he hopes Haaland and Cherki both get a breather in the cup.
quote: I'm looking for clues from Maresca and assuming that those who didn't start that match will probably start this one. So I hope Holland gets a break, Cherki gets a break.

claim: Lateriser rates Bruno Fernandes as a key differential for his Free Hit team given Man Utd's home game vs Fulham, saying few Free Hit managers will have both Bruno and Haaland this week.
quote: Bruno Fernandes is the difference against Fulham. I like it... you still have Bruno and Holland. I don't think there will be many managers who have both of them for these two good matches.

claim: João Pedro is the only player Lateriser is carrying over from his existing squad into his Free Hit team.
quote: First of all, are there any players from your current roster remaining on the team for Free Hit? Yes, one... it has to be João Pedro, obviously.

claim: Lateriser is considering Solanke for his Free Hit team and says he is now unsure whether Solanke is even a Wildcard must-have despite calling him a full-season player last week.
quote: Now the question is whether to take Solanke for Free Hit, because he is quite an interesting option. I'm not even sure if he's a Wild Card must-win, despite me saying last week that he looks like a full-season player.

claim: Lateriser confirms Calafiori and João Pedro are locks in his Free Hit team.
quote: I would definitely take Calafiori... So I imagine you have Calafiori and João Pedro. Yes.

claim: Lateriser includes Haaland in his Free Hit team, arguing City's attacking depth everywhere except Haaland's own position (cover from Doku, Cherki, Foden etc.) only strengthens Haaland himself as the fixed spearhead, and Man Utd's defensive fragility adds insurance value.
quote: There are so many great players around him, and he remains the spearhead of this attack... the 'crumble' factor at United is a bit too high... it is just some insurance to protect ourselves.

claim: Lateriser says he can leave Gabriel out of his Free Hit team without needing the extra money freed up, since Haaland remains his highest-potential pick regardless.
quote: If you can do without Gabriel on your free-throw, you don't really need the money, and I feel like Holland still has the highest potential.

claim: Lateriser rates Szoboszlai as a high-floor 'glue' pick with guaranteed minutes even at right-back, arguing his move to right-back (with Araujo covering rather than Frimpong) actually increases his attacking freedom higher up the pitch, and that he is the league's best set-piece taker: two free-kick goals, five or six assists from set pieces, and three or four penalties this season already.
quote: He's kind of like the glue for your squad... he's also just the best set piece taker in the league... Two free-kick goals this season. Five or six assists from set pieces this season. Three or four goals from penalties this season.

claim: Lateriser notes Szoboszlai previously had to cover right-back defensively when Frimpong played there, but with Araujo now in that slot he has more license to push forward.
quote: Before, when Frimpong was there, he had to cover the right-back position. But if we have Araujo in that position, it gives him a little bit more freedom to operate up front.

claim: Lateriser names Palmer as his Free Hit captain ahead of João Pedro, expecting Chelsea to dominate possession against Hull's deep back-three low block -- suiting Palmer's ability to shoot from outside the box -- while João Pedro could get bogged down against a packed defence.
quote: Palmer has the space to shoot long and dictate the game from outside the box, and he likes that kind of deep defence... Palmer will be my captain.

claim: Lateriser locks in Rogers as Chelsea's third attacking pick for his Free Hit team, reasoning that if Chelsea have a big win he wants exposure to whichever of the front three gets the brace, rather than only owning the two 'best' options.
quote: Triple choice in Chelsea's attack... the advantage of a three-point attack is that... you don't know which of the three players is going to score a brace. So you put yourself in a position where you are guaranteed to get that brace.

claim: Jack (host) questions whether Estêvão will eat into the front three's minutes off the bench; Lateriser says Rogers is the one of the trio most likely to be the one withdrawn around the 70-75 minute mark, and would sell him only once he sees that happen in back-to-back games.
quote: You see him coming off the pitch for 70-75 minutes two games in a row -- then sell him. Until then, his playing time looks consistent.

claim: Lateriser applies the same logic to Welbeck and Mitoma -- treat them as safe, consistent starters and only worry about their minutes once there is actual evidence of a problem.
quote: Welbeck and Mitoma are only a problem when they become a problem. Until then you can count on them.

claim: Lateriser says his final Liverpool picks depend on midweek European minutes: he currently prefers Gakpo over Wirtz, but would get worried if Gakpo plays a full 90 in the Wednesday Atletico match, and would consider swapping in Barcola if he gets meaningful minutes off the bench that game.
quote: My Liverpool picks will pretty much be made up after Wednesday night when they finish playing Atletico. I want to see who gets how many minutes. If Gakpo plays 90 minutes, I'll be a little worried.

claim: Lateriser says Liverpool's fixture is the core reason he is using the Free Hit at all, since he does not currently own Isak; he plans to sell Bruno Fernandes for Palmer two weeks before wildcarding, and does not rate Liverpool assets as good holds beyond this week because tougher fixtures follow.
quote: Liverpool is the reason I use Free Hit, because right now I just... I don't have him in my team... I don't think Liverpool's players are a good choice after this week because they have tough games coming up.

claim: Jack (host) says Lateriser's Free Hit rating jumped from 82% (his real team) to 93% with this Free Hit XI.
quote: You've gone from 82% in your regular team to 93%. That's a huge boost.

claim: Lateriser says if he goes with the Free Hit this week he would keep his existing wildcard in reserve and revert to his old squad in Gameweek 5, using his one free transfer only if Foden picks up an injury.
quote: I'll probably use it if Foden is injured, otherwise I wouldn't use it at all.

claim: Jack says the Free Hit decision partly hinges on a player's absence, reporting he skipped training ahead of the weekend fixture, with a positive update possible from a pre-match press conference.
quote: It will all depend a bit on how long Nicolo Ali is out. Today there was news that he didn't train before the game.

claim: Discussing last week's results, the pair note Sangaré was substituted in the 45th minute, taken as an early sign Newcastle-facing opponents (defensively) are not the most reliable.
quote: Sangare was substituted in the 45th minute. Does this mean anything?

claim: Both agree Konsa at 4.5m is a near-mandatory pick given Arsenal's double clean sheet threat, arguing his price undersells him relative to a defender who should really cost 5.5m, freeing budget elsewhere; his display against Chelsea was rated outstanding.
quote: Konsa is just a gift for 4.5 million... his performance against Chelsea was outstanding... Konsa is a gift that you should use when forming a squad.

claim: In a hypothetical Round-5-onward Wildcard scenario, Lateriser would still keep this attacking core (Haaland, Palmer, João Pedro, Rogers) and is tempted to squeeze in Bruno Fernandes too, with compromises required elsewhere.
quote: Gonzalo would be there, Haaland would be there, Pedro would be there, Palmer would be there, Rodgers probably too. I was wondering if I could squeeze Bruna in.

claim: In the hypothetical Wildcard version, Lateriser would prefer Vuskovic over De Cuyper as the more stable long-term Brighton defensive option.
quote: Vuskovic instead of De Cuyper, just as a much more stable option in the longer term.

claim: Lateriser would include a Spurs defender such as Van Hecke in his hypothetical Wildcard side.
quote: There would be a Spurs defender like Van Hecke, probably.

claim: Lateriser would swap in Egan over O'Shea on a hypothetical Wildcard, rating Egan the best 4m defender in the game given Hull's fixture list, and prefers O'Shea over Davis as his 4m enabler in the meantime.
quote: It would be Egan instead of O'Shea, just because I think he's the best defender for 4 million in the game. And Hull have a good fixture list.

claim: Lateriser floats adding a cheap Man Utd defensive enabler such as Shaw plus another defender from Liverpool or Chelsea in order to keep a struggling forward such as Jota in his hypothetical squad -- attribution uncertain given the interview's heavy translation garbling and the corpus's known Shaw/Thiaw caption confusion.
quote: I'm tempted to maybe replace one of those attacking players, take Shaw, take Shaw and add a defender from Liverpool or Chelsea.

claim: BigManBakar is actively considering activating his Triple Captain chip this week but has not decided; he says he has not had much time to think about FPL after a tough week.
quote: It's definitely being considered. I'm currently hesitating whether to use it or not.

claim: BigManBakar defends last week's decision to Wildcard rather than hold, saying his wildcard team was built to be low-maintenance so he could bank transfers and go on autopilot for two or three weeks until Gameweek 6 or 7.
quote: My wildcard team was built with the idea of creating a solid roster that would allow me to save as many transfers as possible for a certain amount of time.

claim: BigManBakar says he does not regret last week's Wildcard even though his old team without it would probably have scored more, because that outcome (an unpredictable Le Fée/Enzo-type penalty, a blank week from almost every popular player) could not have been foreseen at the deadline; he judges chip decisions by the information available at the time, not by hindsight.
quote: I don't regret the wild card decision at all, because I think it made sense for my team... I don't view the outcome as a way to assess the success or failure of my decision.

claim: BigManBakar cites an unpredictable penalty goal from Enzo as an example of the kind of randomness that swung last week's scores.
quote: Enzo Le Fe scored a penalty, something no one could have predicted.

claim: BigManBakar cites an unpredictable penalty goal from Le Fée as an example of the kind of randomness that swung last week's scores.
quote: Enzo Le Fe scored a penalty, something no one could have predicted.

claim: BigManBakar says he is glad he avoided Man City's rotation-risk attackers last week, since apart from Haaland none of them looked like a realistic long-term hold given how unpredictable their minutes are.
quote: Apart from Holland, none of them looked like a realistic long-term option. Playing time is just too questionable or unstable to predict.

claim: BigManBakar's wildcarded-in Schär scored an unlucky own goal last week, which he says frustrated him in the moment.
quote: Cedar scored an own goal. I was pretty angry when it happened.

claim: BigManBakar changed his wildcard plan before the deadline, dropping a version that had included Calafiori and Anderson.
quote: I changed the version with Calafiori and Elliot Anderson that I showed in the previous video to this one.

claim: BigManBakar says he dropped Calafiori-funded O'Reilly before the deadline after City-fan contacts were split on whether he'd play; O'Reilly did start but was injured in the warm-up, and BigManBakar says there is no guarantee he plays in the coming weeks.
quote: He eventually started, but was injured during warm-ups, but I can say with complete confidence that there are no guarantees that he will play in the coming weeks.

claim: Unable to afford O'Reilly, BigManBakar weighed Saka against Martinelli and picked Saka, banking on Konsa (with Saliba as a fallback) to cover Arsenal's defence, and liking that Saka freed up money to bring in Bruno Fernandes later if needed.
quote: I settled on Sakho because I thought I could cover Arsenal's defense with Ryan Konsa and then switch to Saliba if needed... Saka would be a great way to save money, allowing me to easily buy Bruno Fernandes if needed.

claim: Jack (host) says he is 90% likely to wildcard this week too, and expects his team to differ from BigManBakar's by only five or six players, with the same core (Saka, Palmer, Haaland, João Pedro).
quote: I'm 90% going to use the wildcard this week. And my team doesn't look that different from yours... I think I'll have Saka, Palmer, of course, Holland, of course... Joao Pedro is there too.

claim: BigManBakar says he will definitely captain Palmer this week, expecting Hull's clean-sheet run to regress (their underlying numbers do not support three clean sheets), and will watch Palmer's minutes in the midweek EFL Cup tie vs Leeds for a green light on the Triple Captain.
quote: I will definitely make Palmer captain because he is in the squad and the match against Hull City is quite normal... I'll keep an eye on Palmer's playing time tonight. Chelsea play Leeds United in the EFL Cup.

claim: BigManBakar is weighing Triple Captain Palmer this week against saving it for Haaland at home to Ipswich in Gameweek 7 or Hull in Gameweek 16, but rules out GW16 as too far away to plan around, and is torn between Haaland's home fixture and Man City's European rest risk around it.
quote: I have to consider Holland in Round 7 against Ipswich at home or Round 16 against Hull at home as real options... excluding MX16, I view the fourth and seventh rounds as more realistic windows.

claim: BigManBakar is wary that Haaland's Gameweek 7 home fixture against Ipswich sits between two midweek European games (PSG then Athens), and though he expects a Premier League start, the manager's minutes-management comments make an early substitution on Triple Captain week a real risk.
quote: It's between two matches in Europe. One seems to be against PSG, the other against Athens... any early substitution would be a huge setback for the triple captain.

claim: Both discuss effective ownership: Haaland's triple-captain EO was around 235% last week, meaning heavy triple-captain use made his high score less of a relative gain, while Palmer's ownership is currently 22% and his effective ownership this week is expected to stay under 100%, which appeals to BigManBakar as a more differential Triple Captain pick.
quote: 235? Okay. Well, to explain what that means: it was actually owned by 235% of the people... His ownership is now 22%. It may not be higher than 100.

claim: BigManBakar leans toward a midfielder for Triple Captain generally, reasoning Palmer's scoring floor is higher (a goal plus clean sheet and bonus gets him to a strong score easily) even though Haaland is statistically more likely than Palmer to score at all in his own fixture.
quote: I am always a little more comfortable having a midfielder as a triple captain... You need two goals from Holland to get 12-13 points, while Palmer can do it quite easily even with one goal.

claim: BigManBakar says he is 50/50 on pulling the Triple Captain trigger on Palmer, framing it as a risk/reward call versus the worst case of Haaland scoring big while Palmer blanks, and says he will decide close to the deadline after checking Palmer's cup minutes tonight.
quote: I'm leaning towards 50/50 for now... I would really expect that from him. Let's see.

claim: BigManBakar says Fantasy Football Hub's AI transfer tool is recommending no transfers for his team this week despite having two free transfers banked, which matches his own plan after the wildcard.
quote: You have two free transfers, but the AI recommends not making any, which is exactly what you want to see.

claim: BigManBakar is glad Konsa started the pre-season/warm-up game, taking it as a sign he is becoming a real option for his XI.
quote: I'm really glad Konsa started the pre-game. He will become a real option for me.

claim: BigManBakar likes Wan-Bissaka at home to Everton, expecting Everton's attack to be weaker without a key player.
quote: Wan-Bissaka looks like a good choice at home against Everton. I think Everton's attack won't be as good.

claim: BigManBakar is unsure whether Sangaré's early substitution last week was down to a yellow card or a genuinely poor performance, and is leaving him on the bench this week as a precaution while still rating his long-term Defcon upside highly.
quote: Sangare is the only one of my eight attacking players that I'm really worried about... he showed that his Defcon rate over 90 minutes is just insane.

claim: BigManBakar confirms his Gameweek 4 XI is a 3-4-3 with no transfers, captaining Palmer, and can bench both his Newcastle players for their away trip to Leeds since he expects Leeds to score.
quote: So a 3-4-3 formation with Palmer as captain, no transfers, and then we'll be back to business in round five.

claim: In a hypothetical Wildcard this week, BigManBakar says he would take Rogers over Saka and fund an Arsenal defender with the money saved, rating Rogers at 7.5-7.6m a great price given nailed minutes and no European-competition rotation risk.
quote: If I was using the chip this week, I would probably take Rodgers and use the money to sign the Arsenal defender... Rodgers at 7.5 or 7.6 is a really good choice because he's not risky in terms of playing time.

claim: BigManBakar names Anderson as the one Man City midfielder he would consider given the Chelsea League Cup tie removing some rotation uncertainty.
quote: If anyone has a City midfielder, then in my opinion, Turchi, Foden or Rodgers are a great choice.

claim: BigManBakar argues owning three Chelsea attackers is not a reason to avoid captaining or Triple Captaining Palmer -- he judges each decision on its own merits rather than worrying about covariance within his own squad.
quote: Just because you have three Chelsea attacking players doesn't mean you shouldn't make Palmer captain or triple captain... I believe that you should evaluate each decision on its merits.

claim: BigManBakar says he will trigger the Triple Captain on Palmer if he gets some rest in the EFL Cup game tonight (a substitution around the 60th minute would count as reassuring; playing over 80 minutes would be a red flag), while expecting him to start.
quote: I think if Palmer gets some rest today, I'll be all for it... if he plays, say, over 80 minutes, that would be a red flag, in my opinion.

claim: BigManBakar's hypothetical wildcard goalkeeper would be Verbruggen instead of Raya, used as a budget enabler.
quote: I also have Verbruggen instead of Rai.

claim: BigManBakar's hypothetical wildcard would include Calafiori.
quote: Calafiori instead of Malacia.

claim: BigManBakar names Hall and Van Hecke as defenders he would include on a hypothetical wildcard, still weighing Vuskovic or a Leeds defender (name mangled in captions, resolved via context) as further options.
quote: Hall and Van Hecke are the ones I'm considering, as are Viskovic or Mihajlovic.

claim: Focal notes Isak scored two goals from just 0.21 combined expected goals in Liverpool's 2-0 win over Ipswich -- a well above-expected return.
quote: Only 0.21 expected goals in total, so pretty poor from Sheringham.

claim: Focal says it was a painful week for managers who sold Isak on the wildcard with a view to swapping in Haaland, since that trade made sense in principle but backfired against Ipswich.
quote: Painful one if you sold Isak, like many did on the wildcard with a view to swapping Haaland in.

claim: Focal reports Szoboszlai was denied a big first-half penalty shout (which he would presumably have taken) and then won a second-half penalty himself, though Isak -- who would have taken it -- was already off the pitch, and it was ruled out for offside in the build-up anyway.
quote: There was a really huge penalty shout right before half-time not given, which presumably Szoboszlai would have taken... second half as well, Szoboszlai won a penalty himself. Isak was off the pitch at that point and he definitely would have taken it, but it was offside in the build-up.

claim: Focal notes Araujo started at right-back ahead of Szoboszlai (contrary to some expectations) and had a decent game.
quote: Araujo started in right back, not Szoboszlai which some thought might happen. He had a decent game actually.

claim: Focal says Wirtz was unlucky to blank, having actually registered an assist that was chalked off for offside.
quote: Verts really unlucky though. He did actually have an assist, but it was chalked offside.

claim: Focal thinks Gakpo and Barcola could become a lethal winger pairing (Gakpo right, Barcola left); Barcola started on the bench, came on and looked sharp, breezing past defenders.
quote: He could actually be a really lethal winger pairing with Barcola probably coming in left wing, Gakpo right wing from now on.

claim: Focal says it is too early to buy Barcola at 8m and prefers a wait-and-see approach.
quote: It's too early to buy in my opinion. I think he's a wait and see, especially for 8 mil.

claim: Focal's wildcarded-in Schär scored an unlucky own goal in Newcastle's 2-2 draw with Bournemouth that he says he could not have done anything about.
quote: This one was a painful one in my team having wildcarded Schar in, who scored an incredibly unlucky own goal that he couldn't have done anything about.

claim: Focal says Hall would have been the better pick over Schär -- no own goal, and he came away with an assist instead.
quote: I'd have you opted for Hall instead, who didn't score a lone goal and he came away with an assist.

claim: Focal highlights Scott's back-to-back 10 and 12 point hauls and 11/15/11 Defcon-relevant defensive actions across the first three games, saying he is flying under the radar at 6m.
quote: That's 10 and 12 points as back-to-back. I think he's really going under the radar for 6 mil. 11, 15, and 11 Defcons as well.

claim: Focal says Bournemouth's fixtures look rougher on the FDR colour scale than they actually are, listing Brentford (h), Liverpool (h), Chelsea (a), Sunderland (h) and Man Utd (a), and flags their Gameweek 7-onward run as particularly good.
quote: The fixtures do look a little bit rough, but not as bad as they seem based on the FDR colors.

claim: Focal rates Silva at 5m as a great defensive option, having hit Defcon in two of his first three games, and is eyeing him for when Bournemouth's fixtures turn from Gameweek 7.
quote: I think Silva for 5 mil looks like a great option in defense. He hit Defcon in two of the first three games.

claim: Focal names Thiaw (captioned 'Chou') as a safe, reliable pick worth recommending.
quote: Chou and Hoilett are safe, reliable picks. I would recommend them.

claim: Focal notes Wissa picked up a booking (costing a point) but is still worth considering around 6.1-6.2m.
quote: Wissa got booked, one point off him, but he's still worth looking at even for I think he's 6.1 mil now, maybe 6.2.

claim: Focal reports Osula (captioned 'Sola') is currently injured.
quote: There is Fernandes Pardo. And of course there's Sola as well. Sola's currently injured.

claim: Focal expects Wissa to play as a withdrawn '10' with Fernandez-Pardo as the central '9', and does not see Wissa dropping deeper as a negative.
quote: I think what will likely happen is Wissa plays as a 10, which I don't think is a bad thing... and Pardo playing as the number nine.

claim: Focal reports Donnarumma made several important saves to preserve Man City's 1-0 clean sheet against a Coventry side that had a good game and registered 1.4 xG.
quote: Donnarumma made some really big saves to keep the clean sheet.

claim: Focal says Haaland became the most triple-captained player in history last gameweek, and rates his 9-point week as a 'happy middle ground' rather than a clear success or failure, noting he'd ideally want a double-digit return when using the chip.
quote: Haaland became the most triple captain player in history last Gameweek... I think it's in the like not fair but not a big success territory.

claim: Focal reports Foden was benched last gameweek.
quote: Foden benched.

claim: Focal reports Cherki started but blanked.
quote: Cherki started and he came away with a blank as well.

claim: Focal reports Udogie was set to start but withdrew with a back issue before kickoff.
quote: Udogie was set to start but he dropped out of a back issue.

claim: Focal reports Enzo came into the side and made his debut.
quote: Which meant Enzo came into the team for his debut.

claim: Focal cites Maresca's reputation for heavy rotation at Chelsea last season (85 changes in all competitions by November, far more than any other club) plus the current squad's attacking depth as reasons he will avoid Chelsea's non-front-three City-style rotation risk in Man City's case, saying he is only avoiding Man City's attackers, of whom he'd only consider Anderson.
quote: Last season up until November in all comps he'd made 85 changes at that point. Significantly more than any other team... I'm going to be avoiding the City attackers. I think the only mid I would consider is Anderson.

claim: Focal says Anderson might be the best points-per-million long-term pick among Man City attackers, calling him a 'Rolls-Royce player' after another good game.
quote: I do think Anderson might be the best bet in terms of points per million long-term. Just absolute Rolls-Royce player.

claim: Focal presents his statistical Team of the Week for the upcoming gameweek: Raya, Gabriel, Van Hecke, Palmer, Rogers, Saka, Szoboszlai, Wirtz, Isak and João Pedro, with Kinsky, Vuskovic and Disasi on the bench, and says on a wildcard there is even a case for no Haaland given Chelsea's fixture vs Hull.
quote: It's Raya, the keeper, Gabriel, Van Hecke, Palmer, Rodgers, Saka, Szoboszlai, Wirtz, Isak and Joao Pedro... I think actually on a wildcard as well you can make a case for no Haaland especially when you've got Chelsea home to Hull.

claim: Focal's statistical Team of the Week bench is Kinsky, Vuskovic and Disasi.
quote: And a bench of Kinski, Vuskovic, Disasi and Balogun.

claim: Focal says he would personally swap Wirtz for Gakpo in that statistical team.
quote: I think I'd also go Gakpo over Wirtz but other than that it looks about spot on.

claim: Focal says Hull have kept three clean sheets despite conceding over five expected goals -- clearly unsustainable -- and that there is 'just no way' he is not captaining a Chelsea player (Palmer or João Pedro) against them this week, despite Haaland's excellent historical record against Man Utd.
quote: I know Hull have kept three clean sheets which in itself is unbelievable with just over five xG conceded. There's just no way that I'm not captaining a Chelsea player next week.

claim: Focal ranks projected goals over the next five fixtures: Man City top, then Chelsea, Liverpool, Arsenal, Man Utd, Newcastle, Brentford, Brighton, Bournemouth, and Fulham.
quote: Man City are top with projected goals followed by Chelsea, then it's Liverpool, Arsenal, Man United, Newcastle, Brentford, Brighton, Bournemouth, and Fulham.

claim: Focal ranks the projected clean-sheet ticker over the next five fixtures: Arsenal top, then Man City, Chelsea, Newcastle, Brighton, Forest, Spurs, Man Utd, Everton, and Fulham.
quote: The clean sheets ticker has got Arsenal top, and then it's Man City, Chelsea, Newcastle, Brighton, Forest, Spurs, Man United, Everton, and Fulham.

claim: Focal rates Semenyo as probably the safest Man City attacker after Haaland himself.
quote: Semenyo probably the safest after Haaland, maybe Enzo as well if you want to risk it.

claim: Focal says Fulham have lost their opening three games for only the third time in the club's history and expects wide-open, high-scoring games; he likes Castagne for attacking returns but says to avoid Fulham defensively otherwise.
quote: I think Castagne looks good, but defensively definitely avoid. They're looking vulnerable.

claim: Focal notes Fulham's next two fixtures are Liverpool and Man Utd, meaning their defensive numbers could get even worse before their run against three promoted teams.
quote: Liverpool and Man United are Fulham's next two fixtures, so could it get even worse?

claim: Focal says Martinez, Chelsea's new number one, could be a shout at 5m.
quote: Martínez I think could be a shout for 5 million goals, their new number one.

claim: Focal says Chilwell is worth a look despite the -1 for his own goal, projecting he should earn more Defcons than Hall over the season.
quote: Despite the minus one pointer for the own goal, Chilwell is worth looking at. He should earn more def cons than Hall over the season.

claim: Focal reports Brighton's first-choice goalkeeper is a bigger risk now with an ongoing issue, should be benched for the Arsenal fixture, and per manager Hürzeler is targeted to return after the international break (Gameweek 6), possibly for the Sunderland game.
quote: The keeper is a little bit more of a risk now. He does have commentary, and then you'd bench him against Arsenal, and you might get that Sunderland game in Gameweek 6... All that Hürzeler has said is he's back after the international break, which is Gameweek 6.

claim: Focal likes Van Hecke, now down to 4.9m, citing just 1.65 expected goals conceded over his last two games, a nailed starting spot, an 8-point haul last match, and a fixture run of Everton (h), Villa (h), Man Utd, Coventry (h), Chelsea (a) -- he'd bench him for the Man Utd and Chelsea games specifically and start him the rest, and rates Spurs' fixtures beyond that (Palace, Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham) as excellent.
quote: Only 1.65 expected goals conceded over the last two. I think people are sleeping on Spurs defensively a little bit. He's dropped to 4.9 mil as well now. Nailed in every game, eight points in the last match.

claim: Focal reports Maitland-Niles came on for his Everton debut and scored a last-minute long-range curling winner-equaliser to rescue a draw against Man Utd.
quote: Maitland-Niles comes on for his debut. Last minute of the game, he hits it from miles out, and it curls top corner.

claim: Focal reports George also scored for Everton in the same game.
quote: George also rocketed one past Lamela.

claim: Focal reports Mbeumo and Šeško were the other scorers for Man Utd in the draw at Everton.
quote: Other scorers were Mbeumo and Sesko.

claim: Focal notes Shaw registered his first assist since Gameweek nine of last season.
quote: Shaw getting his first assist since Gameweek nine last season.

claim: Focal notes Maguire hit the Defcon threshold in the Everton game.
quote: Maguire and Tarkowski hit Defcon.

claim: Focal notes Tarkowski hit the Defcon threshold in the same game, but says he would avoid him at 5.5m.
quote: Maguire and Tarkowski hit Defcon. Man U did as well, and he got an assist for a nine-pointer, but I would avoid him for 5.5 mil.

claim: Focal reports Bruno Fernandes blanked (just 2 points) despite assisting the assister for Šeško's goal.
quote: So, Bruno blanks as well. Just wasn't his day. He did assist the assister for Sesko's goal, but two-pointer.

claim: Focal notes it was almost inevitable that Mbeumo would score and get a bonus point right after being the most sold player in the world last gameweek, with 750,000 net transfers out.
quote: How inevitable was it that Mbeumo scored and got a bonus point after being the most sold player around the world last Gameweek. 750,000 net transfers out.

claim: Focal notes most of the managers who sold Mbeumo bought Cherki, who went on to blank.
quote: Of course, the vast majority of those buying Cherki, goes on to blank.

claim: Focal highlights another double-digit haul for Ødegaard, his second in three gameweeks, noting he already has two Premier League goals this season versus just one in 24 appearances all last season, calling him a potential bargain at 6.6m.
quote: That's another double-digit return from him, two in the first three Gameweeks... he's doubled his Premier League goal tally from the entirety of last season, where he got one in 24. Looks a potential bargain for 6.6 mil.

claim: Focal rates Raya as likely to be the top-scoring goalkeeper this season.
quote: You've got Raya, he's probably going to be the top scoring keeper this season.

claim: Focal rates Arsenal's defensive options highly across the board: Calafiori and Gabriel for goal threat, and Konsa as a standout at 4.4m.
quote: You've got Calafiori and his goal threat, Gabriel's goal threat, his nailedness, defcons... You've got Consa for 4.4 mil.

claim: Focal notes Tzolis picked up another assist.
quote: Zolis with another assist.

claim: Focal says Rice got an assist and is just one Arsenal home fixture (vs Hull) away from being back in the conversation as a pick, noting he was a great choice last season too.
quote: Rice got an assist as well. Like, Rice is one whole next Gameweek away from being right back in the conversation. He was a great pick last season as well.

claim: Focal notes Havertz now has two goals in three games.
quote: Havertz has got two goals in three.

claim: Focal says Chelsea played well and battled to the end in their loss to Arsenal, and that he is hoping to hold Palmer and João Pedro for the long term.
quote: I think they're going to have a great season and I'm hoping to hold on to Palmer and Joao Pedro very long term.

claim: Focal reports Suzuki kept a clean sheet in Villa's 0-0 draw with Hull for a 10-point haul, calling it an early sign he is a good goalkeeper signing.
quote: Suzuki kept a clean sheet versus Hull. So, 10 pointer from him... Early signs are Suzuki looks like a really good signing.

claim: Focal says Egan and Mendy look like great budget Hull defenders given their run of clean sheets and defensive-contribution numbers.
quote: The likes of Egan, Mendy looking like great budget defenders, loads of defcons.

claim: Focal notes Vuskovic scored for Brighton, adding to a 10-point haul.
quote: Vaskovic as well, he scored for Brighton. Can we have a 10 point haul himself?

claim: Focal notes a wild 14-point haul from Bogle.
quote: Bogel with a mad 14 pointer.

claim: Focal notes Mitchell scored a brace for a 15-point haul.
quote: Mitchell scored a brace 15 pointer.

claim: Focal notes only three forwards scored a goal across the entire gameweek: Haaland, Isak, and Šeško off the bench.
quote: Only three forwards in total scored a goal this Gameweek. That was Haaland, Isak and then Sesko off the bench.

claim: Focal is frustrated Thiago blanked again despite a great home fixture vs Sunderland and 2.4 expected goals without scoring, and thinks he is starting to look like a sell as Brentford's fixtures turn tougher (Bournemouth, Chelsea, Villa, Liverpool).
quote: Great fixture home to Sunderland... 2.4 xGs registered, yet to score... the fixtures are turning now, so he's looking like a sell.

claim: Focal notes Williams finished on seven points and was unlucky to have a goal ruled out for handball after the ball hit his hand while he was protecting his face from a boot.
quote: Williams finished on seven points and he was really unlucky to have a goal ruled out for handball.

claim: Focal reveals his own Gameweek 4 team: a 3-4-3 of Raya; Van Hecke, De Cuyper, Konsa; Saka, Foden, Szoboszlai, Groß; Haaland, Wissa, João Pedro, with M.Sangaré on the bench.
quote: So, let's have a look at my team selection for Gameweek 4. I'm lined up with Raya in goal. It's a 3-4-3. It's Van Hecke, De Cuyper, and Konsa in defense. Saka, Foden, Szoboszlai, and Gross in midfield. Haaland, Wissa, and João Pedro up front.

claim: Focal benches Sangaré on his own bench this week.
quote: And on the bench, Bentley, Sangaré, Tchouaméni.

claim: Focal deliberately left 3.3m in the bank on his wildcard specifically to fund a planned Foden-to-Palmer transfer in Gameweek 4, and will make Palmer captain with João Pedro as vice-captain.
quote: I left myself with 3.3 million in the bank on the wildcard intentionally. And that's to leave enough money for Foden to Palmer in Gameweek 4... And then captain Palmer. So, João Pedro becomes vice-captain then.

claim: Focal explains he nearly picked Spence instead of Mendy for his fifth defender slot and also considered Ajer, but chose Mendy to preserve future flexibility since most other budget (4.5m) defenders are weak this year while there are plenty of good options at 5m-plus.
quote: I very nearly opted for Djed Spence instead of Mendy for that fifth defender spot. I also looked at Ajer... Instead I went for Mendy as my fifth defender.

claim: Focal says he nearly picked Spence over Mendy for his fifth defender slot, and also considered Ajer, before settling on Mendy to preserve budget flexibility.
quote: I very nearly opted for Djed Spence instead of Mendy for that fifth defender spot.

claim: Focal says the 0.7m left in the bank after his Foden-to-Palmer move lets him upgrade De Cuyper or Konsa to any 5m-plus defender if needed.
quote: That allows, you know, Konsa or De Cuyper to any defender that's 5 mil or over. And there's way more good picks at 5 mil and over in terms of defenders.

claim: Focal's longer-range plan is to start De Cuyper this week, bench him against Arsenal, start him again versus Sunderland in Gameweek 6, then swap to Silva once Bournemouth's fixtures turn.
quote: The hope is that I can play De Cuyper this week against Coventry. Bench him against Arsenal. Start him against Sunderland in Gameweek 6. And then the swap to Silva lines up perfectly there when Bournemouth's fixtures turn.

claim: Focal flags a contingency that Mitoma might still be out by Brighton's Gameweek 7 home game vs Palace, in which case he would rather roll a transfer than sell De Cuyper.
quote: Brighton have got Palace home in Gameweek 7. So, on the off chance Mitoma is still out, I like rolling for another week thing.
